get.description: Reports that the process is running. Does not check dependencies.
Verifies PostgreSQL and Redis. Returns 503 when any dependency is unavailable.

post.description: Creates the account and signs it in through the same session pipeline as login. Unlike login, this endpoint does disclose whether an email or username is taken — a signup form cannot work otherwise (see ADR-0008).
Returns an identical error for an unknown address and a wrong password, and spends comparable time on both, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which addresses are registered.
Consumes the presented refresh token and issues a new pair. Rotation is single-use: presenting a token that was already rotated is treated as compromise and revokes the whole session.
Revokes this session and its refresh tokens. An access token already issued remains valid until it expires — at most the configured access TTL.
Revokes all sessions for the account, including the one making the request.

get.description: Account identity plus the public profile. Never includes credentials.

patch.description: Only displayName, username and bio are writable in V1. avatarUrl is read-only because object storage does not exist yet.

post.description: Requires the current password. On success **every session is revoked, including this one**, so the client must discard its tokens and sign in again.

get.description: The fixed vocabulary a place can be filed under. Public.

The map query. Returns only what a marker needs — id, name, category and position — so a pan does not transfer descriptions nobody is reading. Viewports crossing the antimeridian are rejected; see the error message.
Nearest first. Distances are metres on the spheroid, not degrees.
Accent- and case-insensitive: "sao paulo" matches "São Paulo". Supply lat/lng to order results by proximity and receive distances.

post.description: Requires a session. Provenance, status and authorship are decided by the server and ignored if sent. The response may carry advisory near-duplicates.

Returns a normalised route between two points: GeoJSON geometry, distance in metres, duration in seconds, bounds computed from the geometry, and legs. Driving only in V1. Nothing is persisted — a route is a computation, not a record.

400.description: Invalid coordinates, or endpoints too close together or too far apart.

422.description: No driving route connects the two points.

502.description: The routing provider is unavailable or returned an unusable result.

504.description: The routing provider exceeded its deadline.

post.description: Calculates the route between two points, finds active Places within the corridor, measures what diverting to each would actually cost, and ranks them by a deterministic, versioned policy. Nothing is persisted: neither the route, the corridor, nor the candidates. An empty candidate list is a successful answer, not an error.

400.description: Invalid coordinates, endpoints too close or too far apart, or a malformed filter.

422.description: No driving route connects the two points, so there is nothing to discover along.

502.description: A routing or travel-cost provider is unavailable or returned an unusable result.

post.summary: Find Places worth considering along a route

post.description: Creates a draft and routes it in the same call. If the routing provider is unavailable the trail is still created without a route snapshot — a draft the user can return to is worth more than an error that loses their two points. `routeIsCurrent` says which happened.
post.summary: Start a trail between two points

get.description: Newest first, keyset-paginated. Summaries only — a list of trails must not ship a LineString per row to a phone.
Everything the builder needs to restore itself from cold: endpoints, ordered stops, the route snapshot, and the revision to send with the next mutation.

404.description: No such trail, or it belongs to someone else — deliberately the same answer.

patch.description: Re-routes the whole composition and recomputes the A → B baseline.

delete.description: Permanent, along with its stops. Acceptable because nothing else references a trail yet — no saves, no shares, no comments.

post.description: A stop is always a resolved Place. The trail is re-routed through it, in position, before anything is written: if routing fails, nothing changes.

409.description: Revision conflict, or that place is already a stop.

422.description: Stop limit reached, or the place cannot be added.

put.description: Takes the whole set in the new order. One call per completed drag — not one per frame — and one recalculation.

400.description: The order omits a stop, repeats one, or names one from another trail.

post.description: Re-asks the provider for the same composition, and refreshes the baseline with it.
Says the user is done composing. **Not publication** — nobody else can see a trail. Requires a route that matches the current composition. Editing a finalized trail returns it to DRAFT.

422.description: The route does not describe the current composition.

post.description: Keeps it, stops listing it by default. The reversible alternative to deleting.

info.title: Trilha API
info.description: Trilha platform API. PR-00 exposes platform endpoints only; product domains are introduced by their own pull requests.

tags.name: platform
tags.description: Liveness, readiness and other operational endpoints

password.description: At least 12 characters. Passphrases are encouraged.

username.description: Letters and numbers, optionally separated by a single - or _.

accessToken.description: Short-lived bearer token for the Authorization header.

refreshToken.description: Opaque, single-use token. Rotated on every refresh; the previous value is invalidated and replaying it revokes the session.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Safe for clients to branch on.

message.description: Human-readable summary. Not intended for end-user display verbatim.

requestId.description: Correlation id for this request. Quote it when reporting problems.

details.description: Optional structured context. Never contains internal details.

refreshToken.description: The opaque refresh token from the previous authentication response.

avatarUrl.description: Always null in V1 — avatar upload is not implemented yet.

currentPassword.description: The password currently on the account.

revokedSessions.description: Sessions revoked by this change. Every session is revoked, including the caller’s, so the client must sign in again.

truncated.description: True when the viewport held more places than the response cap. Zoom in.

distanceMetres.description: Metres from the query point. Null when the query had no reference point.

contributor.description: Public attribution for a community submission. Never an email or account id.

possibleDuplicates.description: Nearby places with a similar name and the same category. Advisory only — the submission was accepted. Two restaurants sharing a name in different places are not duplicates.

placeId.description: Set when this endpoint came from a Place. Routing never requires one.

corridorWidthMeters.description: Corridor half-width in metres. Clamped to the server maximum.

includeCorridor.description: Return the corridor polygon. Off by default: it is a large geometry that clients do not draw.

coordinates.description: GeoJSON positions as [longitude, latitude] — GeoJSON axis order.

geometry.description: GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon covering the area around the route.

corridor.description: Present only when includeCorridor was requested.

corridorWidthMeters.description: Half-width of the search corridor in metres. Clamped to the server maximum. A Place outside it is never considered, however small its detour would be.

maxDetourMinutes.description: Longest acceptable diversion. Candidates costing more are discarded, not ranked lower. Clamped to the server maximum.

categories.description: Place category ids. Empty or absent means every category is eligible.

provenance.description: Where the Place came from. Informational only — it does not affect ranking, because origin is not quality.

distanceFromRouteMeters.description: Shortest distance from the Place to the route line, on the spheroid.

detourDistanceMeters.description: Extra road distance from routing via this Place, against the same provider’s own direct journey. Not the same as distanceFromRouteMeters.

detourDurationSeconds.description: Extra travel time from the diversion.

routeProgress.description: Where along the journey the Place sits: 0 at the origin, 1 at the destination.

relevanceScore.description: How well this Place fits this route, under the named policy. Not a quality rating and not comparable across policy versions.

relevanceReasons.description: Machine-readable codes. Clients own the wording shown to a user.

spatialCandidates.description: Places the spatial query returned, after cheap filters.

evaluatedCandidates.description: Of those, how many had a detour measured.

returnedCandidates.description: How many survived the detour ceiling and were returned.

route.description: The base journey the candidates are measured against.

policyVersion.description: Which ranking policy produced this order. Scores from different versions are not comparable.

revision.description: The trail revision this route describes. Equal to the trail revision means current.
Send this back as expectedRevision on the next mutation.

detour.description: What the stops add over the same endpoints with none. Null when either snapshot is missing — "not measured" is not the same claim as "no detour".

routeIsCurrent.description: Whether the stored route describes the composition as it now stands.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

placeId.description: A stop is always a resolved Place.

source.description: Where the addition came from. Provenance of the composition, not a quality signal.

expectedRevision.description: The revision the client is editing. A mismatch returns 409 rather than overwriting whatever changed in the meantime.

stopIds.description: Every stop on the trail, in the new visiting order.
